title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This page belongs to Grothendieck's study of the 'équation des lacets', the loop relation that an element of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller type, built from (f, alpha, beta), must satisfy.

- Here the relation is projected into 2x2 matrices over Ẑ.
- The fundamental group of P^1 - {0,1,∞} is realised (modulo ±1) as the principal congruence subgroup Γ(2). Its free generators are l_0 = (1 2; 0 1) and l_1 = (1 0; 2 1).
- Its completion maps to (P)SL_2(Ẑ).
- rho is the order-3 automorphism cyclically permuting the three punctures, so rho(l_0) = l_1. sigma_∞ is the involution fixing ∞.
- mu ∈ Ẑ^* is the 'cyclotomic' exponent, with mu = 2nu + 1. eps = eps_2 = ±1 is fixed by mu ≡ eps_2 (mod 4).

Previous page. With xi = alpha rho(alpha)^{-1} and eta = beta sigma_∞(beta)^{-1}, the loop relation becomes (60): xi = eps · eta · l_1^nu.

This page, first part. It makes l_1 explicit as the matrix (1 0; 2 1). Hence (62): l_1^nu = (1 0; 2nu 1) = (1 0; mu-1 1). This is legitimate for nu ∈ Ẑ, since 2nu = mu - 1.

This page, 'Remarques'. A dictionary with the notation of §44 (p. 356 ff.), whose quantities are written with underlines.
- (i) underlined alpha = alpha_0 and underlined beta = beta_0.
- (ii) From p. 357 one normalises beta_0 = 1, i.e. u(sigma_∞) = sigma_∞. Hence beta = f.
- (iii) Formula (17) of §44 gives underlined phi = f sigma_∞(f)^{-1} = eta.
- From (14) of §44, underlined xi = l_0^nu · underlined phi = l_0^nu eta.
- (iv) Comparing with xi = eta l_1^nu (formula (48), stated without the sign eps) gives underlined xi = l_0^nu xi l_1^{-nu} = l_0^nu xi rho(l_0^nu)^{-1}.
- So underlined xi is the rho-twisted conjugate of xi by l_0^nu.
- (v), completed on the next page. Combining with (79) of §44, underlined xi = underlined alpha_0 · rho(underlined alpha_0)^{-1}, gives underlined alpha_0 = l_0^nu alpha.
- Verification: l_0^nu alpha rho(alpha)^{-1} rho(l_0^nu)^{-1} = l_0^nu xi l_1^{-nu}, which matches (iv). Correct.

Purpose. To translate the earlier formalism into a concrete matrix form. The next page writes alpha and beta as Ẑ-matrices and turns the loop relation into explicit quadratic equations in their entries.
errors: The comparison in (iv) uses (48), xi = eta l_1^nu, without the sign eps that appears in (60). This is harmless only modulo ±1 (i.e. in PSL_2) or when eps = 1.
The phrase 'underlined xi est le rho-transformé de l_0^nu' is imprecise. Formula (iv) shows that underlined xi is the rho-twisted conjugate of xi by l_0^nu, not a transform of l_0^nu alone.
There is notational overload. Underlined alpha = alpha_0 in (i), while underlined alpha_0 = l_0^nu alpha in (v); these are different objects but easily confused.

ideas.what: Realising the loops l_0, l_1 around 0 and 1 as the generators (1 2; 0 1) and (1 0; 2 1) of Γ(2), and computing l_1^nu for nu ∈ Ẑ with 2nu = mu - 1.
ideas.modern_name: Γ(2) / Legendre-family uniformisation of π_1(P^1 - {0,1,∞}); congruence quotient of the profinite free group

ideas.what: Dictionary between two notational systems for the solution (f, alpha, beta) of the loop equation, involving twisted conjugation by l_0^nu under the rotation rho.
ideas.modern_name: change of normalisation / cocycle bookkeeping in the Grothendieck–Teichmüller loop (hexagon-type) relation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara for the GT relations

deep.surprise_reason: This is purely notational bookkeeping: a matrix power and a translation table between two sections of the manuscript. The underlying project (the loop equation in matrix form over Ẑ) is of historical interest, but this page adds no new result.
transcription_corrections: The margin label before (iv) is '(iv)', possibly with a stray mark; the final line reads 'comparée à', not 'compariée'.
Line beginning 'Je vais distinguer par des soulignés': it reads roughly 'dans le cas de divergences entre deux notations, les lettres avec la signification attachée dans loc. cit.'
In the next-page continuation, (64) has a crossed-out delta replaced by eps_3, and the delta in (66) is presumably det alpha = eps_3.
